title: Guru Nanak Jayanti 2026: Date, Rituals And 5 Teachings Of Guru Nanak Dev Ji
text:
Guru Nanak Jayanti 2026: Date, Rituals And 5 Teachings Of Guru Nanak Dev Ji
Guru Nanak Jayanti 2026: Celebrate Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s birth on Kartik Purnima with hymns, processions, langar, prayer services and teachings of equality.
Guru Nanak Jayanti, also known as Guru Nanak Gurpurab, holds deep meaning for the Sikh community. The day marks the birth of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, whose teachings on equality, kindness and selfless service still shape lives.
The festival is observed with quiet devotion and collective spirit, not just in India but wherever Sikh communities live. Prayer services, hymn singing, processions and community meals come together to reflect the values Guru Nanak stood for.

Guru Nanak Jayanti Date And Muhurat
In 2026, Guru Nanak Jayanti will be celebrated on Tuesday, November 24. The celebration falls on Kartik Purnima, the full moon day of the Hindu lunar calendar.
- Purnima Tithi begins: 11:42 PM on November 23, 2026
- Purnima Tithi ends: 08:23 PM on November 24, 2026
Since the Purnima tithi covers most of November 24, that day is considered ideal for prayers and observances. Many devotees prefer beginning the day early, during Amrit Vela, which is believed to be especially peaceful and spiritually uplifting.
Why is Guru Nanak Jayanti celebrated
Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born in 1469 in Talwandi, now in Pakistan. Through his travels and teachings, he spread the idea of one universal God and stressed the importance of honest living, equality and helping others. Guru Nanak Jayanti honours his birth and reminds people of values that cut across religion and social status.
Guru Nanak Jayanti: Rituals And Traditions
Celebrations often begin days in advance. Gurdwaras host Akhand Path, a continuous reading of the Guru Granth Sahib. Early morning Prabhat Pheris fill the streets with hymns, while Nagar Kirtans bring communities together in colourful processions. Langar, the free community kitchen, remains central to the day, welcoming everyone without distinction.
5 Core Teachings Of Guru Nanak Dev Ji
- Oneness of God (Ik Onkar): Guru Nanak taught that there is one universal, formless God who is the creator and sustainer of all, beyond gender, caste, or religion.
- Naam Japna – Remembrance of God’s Name: He encouraged constant meditation and remembrance of the Divine Name as a path to spiritual peace and inner purification.
- Kirat Karni – Honest Living: Guru Nanak emphasized earning a living through honest work and integrity, without exploitation or deceit.
- Vand Chhakna – Sharing with Others: He taught the importance of sharing one’s resources and helping those in need, laying the foundation for the community kitchen (Langar).
- Seva (Selfless Service) & Equality: Serving others without expectation and rejecting discrimination based on caste, gender or status were central to his message of universal brotherhood.
Gurpurab: Mantras And Chants
Devotees commonly chant “Sat Sri Akal" and sing Gurbani from the Guru Granth Sahib throughout the day. Hymns praising God’s name and qualities are central to celebrations, reinforcing Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s teachings.
Guru Nanak Jayanti 2026: Dos and Don’ts
Dos:
- Attend early morning prayers (Amrit Vela)
- Participate in kirtans and processions
- Volunteer at langar and community service
- Visit a Gurdwara in clean, modest attire
Don’ts:
- Avoid disrespectful behaviour in sacred spaces
- Do not consume alcohol or meat before visiting Gurdwaras
- Refrain from unnecessary conflict or loud distractions during prayers
Guru Nanak Jayanti 2026: Wishes And Messages
- Happy Guru Nanak Jayanti! May Guru Ji’s blessings fill your life with peace and joy.
- Wishing you and your family a blessed Gurpurab! Dhan Guru Nanak.
- May the divine light of Guru Nanak Dev Ji guide you always. Happy Gurpurab!.
- Nanak Naam Chardi Kala, Tere Bhane Sarbat Da Bhalla! Happy Gurpurab
- On this holy day, let’s embrace Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s timeless teachings of compassion, equality, and unity. Happy Gurpurab!.
- May the divine wisdom of Guru Nanak Dev Ji illuminate your path towards truth, honesty, and selfless service. Happy Nanak Jayanti!.
- Let every step you take echo “Naam Japna, Kirat Karni, Vand Chakna." Wishing you a blessed Gurpurab!.
- May Guru Ji inspire you to live with truth, compassion, and humility, bringing peace and prosperity to all. Happy Gurpurab
- Celebrate this Guru Nanak Jayanti by being a light of compassion in someone’s life.
- May Guru Nanak Dev Ji bless you with the strength to face challenges with patience and faith.
- On this holy day, may your soul be filled with devotion and your heart with love.
- Wishing that Guru Nanak’s teachings guide you through every moment of doubt and darkness.
Guru Nanak Jayanti 2026: FAQs
Why do we celebrate Guru Nanak Jayanti?
Guru Nanak Jayanti celebrates the birth of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikkism.
When Is Guru Nanak Jayanti in 2026?
Guru Nanak Jayanti falls on November 24.
